transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-08
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Carlos, Nina — AtlasForge: Laila, Tom, Jasmine, Matt

Summary: quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + rerank endpoints; showed Console quickstart, demoed a small benchmarks playground, discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs and pilot scope; agreed to POC kickoff and to share security docs.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, rerank endpoint, prefix/KV cache, batching config, evaluation metrics (MRR, nDCG), data residency and SOC2 questions.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approx every 30–60s) ---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood — i'm the AE on the account. quick round robin?
[00:05] Laila: hi, Laila here — head of search at AtlasForge. we build a product search layer for B2B marketplaces.
[00:09] Tom: Tom, data eng. I've got the vector infra and we own ingestion.
[00:12] Jasmine: Jasmine product, i'll be running the success metrics and prioritization.
[00:16] Matt: Matt, ml ops — will own deployment and infra constraints.
[00:20] Carlos: Carlos, software engineer from Redwood, I'll do the technical demo and answer infra questions.
[00:24] Maya: great, quick agenda: show hosted embeddings -> rerank flow, live Console demo, discuss cost/latency and next steps. sound good?
[00:29] Laila: yep, especially curious about rerank scoring and fallback behaviors.
[00:33] Carlos: cool. so we'll start with a tiny demo using the Redwood hosted API. i'll open the Console — you may see a couple of logs as i run a query.
[00:38] [01:05] Carlos: ok opening the Console... (typing) — so the left pane is models/catalog; we recommend using the 4k-embed model for short docs and 8k for longer context. you can see throughput and perf metrics here, and a sample call.
[01:24] Carlos: i'll make a call to /v1/embeddings with a 5-sentence product description.
[01:30] [01:48] Speaker 2: sorry can you slow down - is the embeddings endpoint separate from the rerank?
[01:52] Carlos: yes — embeddings is first: encode query and docs to vectors. rerank is a separate endpoint that accepts a query and candidate docs with their embeddings or raw text. it then returns a score and optional explain field.
[02:10] Maya: one thing AtlasForge asked earlier was about latency; how quick is rerank if we pass precomputed embeddings vs text?
[02:15] Carlos: good question — precomputed embeddings are faster because we skip the embed step. for our hosted API typical median for rerank with embeddings for 50 candidates is ~70-120ms depending on load and model. if you pass raw text and we compute on the fly it adds embed cost so that could be +30–80ms.
[02:36] Tom: what's the cost delta look like? rough per-1k queries?
[02:40] Carlos: rough numbers — embeddings call $X per 1k (placeholder for pricing sheet), rerank per candidate scales a bit; we'll send the exact tiered pricing. but generally precompute + store embeddings is more cost efficient for high QPS.
[02:55] [03:10] Jasmine: do you support batched rerank? like batch 500 queries at once?
[03:14] Carlos: yes, our API supports batching. Redwood Optimize can also suggest batching sizes based on latency SLOs. batching increases throughput but increases tail latency; it's a tunable parameter.
[03:28] Carlos: ok demo time — i'm going to run a sample search: query = "industrial lathe for precision metal" — i'm calling the search pipeline that does retriever -> embeddings distance -> rerank.
[03:40] [03:55] (console output shows timing bars)
[03:58] Carlos: result 1 score 0.84, result 2 score 0.63, see the explain output? it highlights important tokens and gives feature contributions.
[04:10] Laila: the explain looks helpful for product managers. is that explain deterministic?
[04:14] Carlos: it's deterministic for the same model version and input. we also surface feature deltas when you switch model variants.
[04:20] Maya: can you show the blob of candidate embeddings being passed to the rerank endpoint?
[04:23] Carlos: sure (pastes payload) — here's a compressed payload with embeddings vector length 1536. note you can choose float16 quantization on upload to save bytes — we support quantized embeddings storage on Redwood hosted.
[04:38] Matt: about data residency: our legal says customer data must not leave us-east-1. does hosted API respect region pinning?
[04:44] Carlos: yes — we have region routing for hosted customers and can pin to a specific region for storage and inference; for air-gapped or strict residency we also offer Private deployments.
[04:55] [05:05] Laila: SOC2 and KMS for keys?
[05:08] Maya: we'll email SOC2 and KMS/HSM documentation — we also have RBAC and audit logs in the Console.
[05:13] Carlos: for keys we integrate with AWS KMS and customers can rotate keys; logs are exportable to your SIEM.
[05:20] Tom: back to rerank: we have a hybrid pipeline — we use ANN to get top 200, then rerank top 50. is 50 ok? what do you recommend?
[05:26] Carlos: 50 is a solid default. tradeoff: more candidates increases quality but costs more and adds latency. Redwood Optimize can run a small sweep to recommend K (candidates) per QPS and SLO.
[05:36] Jasmine: can we tune for MRR vs precision at 1?
[05:39] Carlos: yes, rerank scoring can be trained/tuned for the metric you care about. we support custom loss tuning via our evaluation harness and you can push the model variant after the POC.
[05:50] [06:10] Carlos: demoing the embeddings upload flow now — you can push bulk vectors via a bulk ingest endpoint, or let us pull from S3 connector. here is a sample curl and a Python snippet in the Console.
[06:25] Speaker 2: is there a connector for Pinecone or Milvus to keep index in sync?
[06:30] Nina: currently we support S3 sync and Kafka connectors; we also have a light-weight adapter pattern for third-party vector DBs but typically customers either use Redwood vector store or a sync pattern. we'll share the connector guide.
[06:45] Tom: our index is very large — 120M docs — does Redwood hosted support that scale?
[06:50] Carlos: hosted can handle multi-tenant large stores but at that scale we often recommend Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. you can start hosted for POC and then migrate to Dedicated.
[07:00] Maya: note also Private if you need on-prem.
[07:03] Laila: what about model drift and re-ranking regressions — how do we detect?
[07:08] Carlos: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring — you can send labeled eval sets and we run regression alerts when a new model variant degrades metrics beyond thresholds. we also provide per-prompt breakdowns.
[07:20] [07:40] Carlos: quick show: i'm running an A/B where we compare the baseline reranker vs a finetuned variant. Console shows delta on MRR and token cost.
[07:55] Jasmine: nice. can we surface business KPIs?
[07:59] Carlos: yes you can map model evals to KPIs in the Console; many customers map to conversion or find-to-cart metrics.
[08:10] Tom: latency SLAs — do you offer SLOs for hosted?
[08:14] Maya: Hosted has best-effort latency targets; Dedicated and Enterprise plans have SLA-backed latency and uptime. we'll include the SLA doc in the follow up.
[08:25] Matt: about fallback strategies — if the preferred model is overloaded can you fallback to a cheaper variant?
[08:29] Carlos: yes — Smart Routing will fallback to compatible model variants or even route to another region. you can define policies per route.
[08:40] [09:00] Laila: curious about the explainability — how much of that is generated vs heuristic scoring?
[09:04] Carlos: a mix: rerank returns learned score plus feature contributions from attention / token overlap heuristics. the explain output is a compact list of top contributing tokens and a confidence bucket.
[09:18] Maya: ok let's walk through a tiny POC plan — goals?
[09:22] Jasmine: primary goal: improve P@1 for B2B part numbers by +8% and not degrade latency beyond 60ms p95.
[09:28] Tom: technical constraints: we need region pinning, keys via KMS, and bulk ingest from S3.
[09:33] Matt: ops: internal firewall and we need a network diagram for our security review.
[09:37] Carlos: proposed POC: 2 weeks run on hosted — week 1 ingest and baseline, week 2 run rerank tuning and quality evals. we'll provide a runbook and sample notebook.
[09:48] Laila: that sounds fine. what's the success criteria?
[09:51] Jasmine: P@1 +8% on withheld eval set, p95 latency < 60ms, and cost per query under our threshold.
[09:58] [10:15] Carlos: logging and traces will be available per-request so you can debug misranks. Console shows token-level cost breakdowns which helps attribution.
[10:30] Maya: ok quick questions from legal we usually get: data retention and deletion — can we purge vectors if requested?
[10:36] Carlos: yes we support granular deletion APIs and retention policies. for private deployments customers have full data control.
[10:42] Tom: how long do embeddings live by default?
[10:45] Nina: default indefinite until you delete; you can set TTL at ingestion time.
[10:50] [11:15] (brief screen share where Carlos runs a curated evaluation harness)
[11:18] Carlos: here's a small eval suite — we run nDCG@10 and MRR. running the finetune variant now, shows +0.06 MRR improvement on the test set.
[11:30] Laila: is that replicable on our data?
[11:33] Carlos: that depends on distribution — we'll run the POC on your sample queries.
[11:38] Jasmine: do you support human-in-the-loop labels? we want to push corrections from SMEs back into the eval harness.
[11:43] Carlos: yes — we have a quick annotation pipeline and can bootstrap model re-ranking with human labels.
[11:50] [12:10] Speaker 2: small nit — you mentioned KV cash earlier? did you mean KV cache?
[12:12] Carlos: yes sorry mis-said, KV cache — it's the prefix/state cache we use for chat but conceptually similar: caching token-level KV helps reduce compute for repeated prefixes.
[12:20] Matt: any guidance on quantized embeddings? we worry about vector precision loss.
[12:24] Carlos: float16/8-bit quantization reduces size; for retrieval it's usually fine but you should test on your top-K recall. Redwood Optimize can simulate quantization impact as part of the POC.
[12:36] [13:00] Maya: wrap up time. recap of commitments?
[13:03] Carlos: we'll send the POC runbook, benchmark checklist, sample curl and python notebooks.
[13:07] Maya: i'll email pricing, contract template, and SOC2/KMS docs.
[13:11] Tom: we'll share 50 labelled queries and a larger 2k unlabeled sample for tuning.
[13:15] Jasmine: schedule POC kickoff in week of Nov 22 — i'll coordinate internally.
[13:20] Laila: thanks all, this was useful. quick note — please include a simple end-to-end example with Python snippets for both embeddings + rerank in the follow up.
[13:30] Carlos: will do.
[13:35] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the items listed. have a good afternoon.

--- End of transcript ---
